sentences.en: TUTOR: Ah ... come in, Russ.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 啊……请进，拉塞尔。

sentences.en: RUSS: Thank you.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 谢谢。

sentences.en: TUTOR: Now you wanted to consult me about your class presentation on nanotechnology - you're due to give it in next week, aren't you?
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 现在你想就纳米技术的课堂展示向我咨询——你下周就要做这个展示，对吧？

sentences.en: RUSS: That's right.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 没错。

sentences.en: And I'm really struggling.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实感到非常吃力。

sentences.en: I chose the topic because I didn't know much about it and wanted to learn more, but now I've read so much about it, in a way there's too much to say - I could talk for much longer than the twenty minutes I've been allocated.
sentences.zh: 我当初选这个主题，是因为自己对此了解不多，想借此多学一些；但现在我已经阅读了大量相关资料，反而觉得内容太多，简直可以说上远超分配给我的二十分钟。

sentences.en: Should I assume the other students don't know much, and give them a kind of general introduction, or should I try and make them share my fascination with a particular aspect?
sentences.zh: 我该假定其他同学对此知之甚少，从而为他们提供一种概括性的入门介绍呢，还是该努力让他们和我一样，对某个特定方面产生浓厚兴趣？

sentences.en: TUTOR: You could do either, but you'll need to have it clear in your own mind.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 两种方式都可以，但你自己必须先明确这一点。

sentences.en: RUSS: Then think I'll give an overview.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 那我想我还是做个概览吧。

sentences.en: TUTOR: OK.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 好的。

sentences.en: Now, one way of approaching this is to work through developments in chronological order.
sentences.zh: 现在，一种切入方式是按时间顺序梳理纳米技术的发展历程。

sentences.en: RUSS: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 嗯。

sentences.en: TUTOR: On the other hand, you could talk about the numerous ways that nanotechnology is being applied.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 另一方面，你也可以围绕纳米技术当前的多种应用展开讲述。

sentences.en: RUSS: You mean things like thin films on camera displays to make them water-repellent, and additives to make motorcycle helmets stronger and lighter.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 您是指比如相机显示屏上的防水薄膜，以及用于提升摩托车头盔强度与轻量化的添加剂之类的应用？

sentences.en: TUTOR: Exactly.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 没错。

sentences.en: Or another way would be to focus on its impact in one particular area, say medicine, or space exploration.
sentences.zh: 又或者，你还可以聚焦于它在某一特定领域（比如医学或太空探索）所产生的影响。

sentences.en: RUSS: That would make it easier to focus.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 这样会更容易集中重点。

sentences.en: Perhaps I should do that.
sentences.zh: 也许我该这么做。

sentences.en: TUTOR: think that would be a good idea.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 我觉得这是个不错的主意。

sentences.en: RUSS: Right.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 好的。

sentences.en: How important is it to include slides in the presentation?
sentences.zh: 幻灯片在展示中有多重要？

sentences.en: TUTOR: They aren't essential, by any means.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 幻灯片绝非必需。

sentences.en: And there's a danger of tailoring what you say to fit whatever slides you can find.
sentences.zh: 而且存在一种风险：你会为了迁就所能找到的幻灯片而刻意调整自己的讲稿内容。

sentences.en: While it can be good to include slides, you could end up spending too long looking for suitable ones.
sentences.zh: 虽然加入幻灯片有时效果不错，但你可能会花太多时间去寻找合适的素材。

sentences.en: You might find it better to leave them out.
sentences.zh: 你或许会发现干脆省略幻灯片反而更好。

sentences.en: RUSS: see.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 明白了。

sentences.en: Another thing I was wondering about was how to start. know presentations often begin with 'First I'm going to talk about this, and then I'll talk about that', but l thought about asking the audience what they know about nanotechnology.
sentences.zh: 我还一直在琢磨开场方式。我知道很多展示通常以‘首先我将讨论这个，然后我将讨论那个’这类句式开头，但我考虑过先问问听众对纳米技术了解多少。

sentences.en: TUTOR: That would be fine if you had an hour or two for the presentation, but you might find that you can't do anything with the it answers you get, and it simply eats into the short time that's available.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 如果你的展示时长有一两个小时，那这样开场当然可以；但你很可能无法有效利用听众给出的回答，结果只是白白消耗掉本就十分有限的时间。

sentences.en: RUSS: So, maybe I should mention a particular way that nanotechnology is used, to focus people's attention.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 那么，也许我该以纳米技术的一项具体应用作为开场，以便迅速抓住大家的注意力。

sentences.en: TUTOR: That sounds sensible.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 听起来很合理。

sentences.en: RUSS: What do you think I should do next?
sentences.zh: RUSS: 接下来您觉得我该做什么？

sentences.en: I really have to plan the presentation today and tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我今天和明天真的必须把整个展示规划出来。

sentences.en: TUTOR: Well, initially I think you should ignore all the notes you've made, take a small piece of paper, and rite a single short sentence that ties together the whole presentation: it can be something as simple as 'Nanotechnology is already improving our lives'.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 好吧，起初我认为你应该暂时抛开所有已做的笔记，拿一张小纸片，用一句简短的话概括整场展示的核心主旨——哪怕像‘纳米技术已在改善我们的生活’这样简单的一句话也行。

sentences.en: Then start planning the content around that.
sentences.zh: 然后围绕这句话来规划具体内容。

sentences.en: You can always modify that sentence later, if you need to.
sentences.zh: 之后如有需要，你随时可以修改这句话。

sentences.en: RUSS: OK.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 好的。

sentences.en: TUTOR: OK, now let's think about actually giving the presentation.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 好的，现在我们来想想实际进行展示时的情况。

sentences.en: You've only given one before, if I remember correctly, about an experiment you'd been involved in.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，你之前只做过一次展示，是关于你参与过的一项实验。

sentences.en: RUSS: That's right.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 没错。

sentences.en: It was pretty rubbish!
sentences.zh: 那次展示简直糟透了！

sentences.en: TUTOR: Let's say it was better in some respects than in others.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 假设它在某些方面表现得更好，而在其他方面则不然。

sentences.en: With regard to the structure, L felt that you ended rather abruptly, without rounding it off Be careful not to do that in next week's presentation.
sentences.zh: 关于结构，L觉得你结束得过于突然，没有进行收尾。下周的演讲中请注意避免这种情况。

sentences.en: RUSS: OK.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 好的。

sentences.en: TUTOR: And you made very little eye contact with the audience, because you were looking.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 而且你与观众几乎没有眼神交流，因为你一直在看……

sentences.en: down at your notes most of the time.
sentences.zh: 大部分时间都低头看着你的讲稿。

sentences.en: You need to be looking at the audience and only occasionally glancing at your notes.
sentences.zh: 你需要面向观众，仅偶尔瞥一眼讲稿即可。

sentences.en: RUSS: Mmm.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 嗯。

sentences.en: TUTOR: Your body language was a little odd.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 你的肢体语言略显奇怪。

sentences.en: Every time you showed a slide, you turned your back on the audience so you could look at it - you should have been looking at your laptop.
sentences.zh: 每次展示幻灯片时，你都会背对观众，转过身去看屏幕——你应该看的是自己的笔记本电脑。

sentences.en: And you kept scratching your head. so I found myself wondering when you were next going to do that, instead of listening to what you were saying!
sentences.zh: 而且你一直挠头，结果我发现自己总在想你接下来什么时候又会挠头，而不是专心听你在说什么！

sentences.en: RUSS: Oh dear.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 哎呀。

sentences.en: What did you think of the language?
sentences.zh: 你觉得语言表达方面怎么样？

sentences.en: I knew that not everyone was familiar with the subject, so l tried to make it as simple as could.
sentences.zh: 我知道并非所有人都熟悉这个主题，所以我尽量把它讲得尽可能简单。

sentences.en: TUTOR: Yes, that came across.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 是的，这一点确实体现出来了。

sentences.en: You used a few words that are specific to the field, but you always explained what they meant, so the audience wouldn't have had any difficulty understanding.
sentences.zh: 你使用了几个该领域的专业术语，但每次都对其含义作了说明，因此观众理解起来应该毫无困难。

sentences.en: Audioscripts
sentences.zh: 听力原文

sentences.en: RUSS: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 嗯。

sentences.en: TUTOR: must say the handouts you prepared were well thought out.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 我必须说，你准备的讲义构思周密。

sentences.en: They were a good summary of your presentation, which people would be able to refer to later on.
sentences.zh: 它们很好地概括了你的演讲内容，听众之后也能随时参考。

sentences.en: So well done on that.
sentences.zh: 这方面做得很好。

sentences.en: RUSS: Thank you.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 谢谢。

sentences.en: TUTOR: Well, I hope that helps you with next week's presentation.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 希望这些建议能帮助你做好下周的演讲。

sentences.en: RUSS: Yes, it will.
sentences.zh: RUSS: 是的，一定会的。

sentences.en: Thanks a lot.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: TUTOR: 'II look forward to seeing a big improvement, then.
sentences.zh: TUTOR: 那我就期待看到显著的进步了。
